death.note: saint.gr heads each of the four «(; - 125)» and dates the occasion of the martyrdom: «Όταν δε, το 125 μ.Χ., ο Κάταλλος απέκτησε γιο, θέλησε να εορτάσουν το γεγονός όλοι οι δούλοι του.» It also places them «στο χρόνια του αυτοκράτορα Αδριανού (117 - 138 μ.Χ.)». No year of birth is printed.

attestations.note: The life page heads «Τύπος εορτής: Σταθερή. Εορτάζει στις 2 Μαΐου εκάστου έτους», the same day as the listing. **This is a company the page enumerates by name**, all four of them, each with his own head line and his own year, so it is four folders and not one: Hesperus, Zoe his wife, and their children Cyriacus and Theodulus. The corpus holds no Hesperus at all, and its Cyriaci and Theoduli are all placed elsewhere; the one Zoe it holds is `zoe-18-december` and is not of Pamphylia. The page names their owners, the Roman Catallus and his wife Petradia, and it records that the emperor Justinian (527–565) raised a church to the martyr Zoe near the church of Saint Anna at the Deuteron of Constantinople, and that Basil I (867–886) rebuilt it from the foundations after it fell — a dedication, and not a relation. It prints no hymn for any of the four and no relic.
